quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #4
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: Where is passing not allowed?

options.text: On hills and curves.
At intersections.
At railroad crossings.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: You cannot pass another vehicle on hills, curves, intersections, or railroad crossings. These are unsafe and illegal places to pass.

questions.question: What should you do before changing lanes?

options.text: Check your mirrors and signal, then change lanes.
Signal, check your mirrors, check your blind spot in the direction you plan to move, then change lanes.
Signal, check your mirrors, and change lanes.
Signal and change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check your mirrors, check your blind spot in the direction you plan to move, then change lanes.
questions.explanation: Turn on your signal first. Then check your rearview and side mirrors. Look over your shoulder to see your blind spot. Make sure no other car is moving into the same lane. Only change lanes when it is safe.

questions.question: What should you do before turning?

options.text: Use your signal.
Turn the wheel.
Increase your speed.
Change lanes.

questions.explanation: Turn on your signal three to four seconds before you turn. This warns other drivers of your plan.

questions.question: You reach an unmarked intersection at the same time as a car on your right. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up and drive through.
Slow down and let the car on your right go first.
Drive into the intersection and make the other car stop.
Honk and drive through.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let the car on your right go first.
questions.explanation: At an unmarked intersection, the car on your right has the right-of-way. Slow down and let it pass safely before you go.

questions.question: How can you prevent hydroplaning?

options.text: Make sure your tires have good tread depth.
Make sure your tires are filled to the right pressure.
Slow down when driving in rain.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Keep your tires in good condition with proper tread and correct air pressure. Slow down when it rains. Hydroplaning happens more often at high speeds on wet roads.

questions.question: How can you make sure your health does not affect your driving?

options.text: Stay in good physical shape and get regular check-ups.
Know how medicines affect your driving.
Drive only within your physical abilities.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Your health is important for safe driving. Know your physical limits. Understand how medicines may affect you. Stay healthy and only drive when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: How much lane space are motorcycles entitled to?

options.text: The bicycle lane.
The same full lane width as other motor vehicles.
Half the width of a lane.
The width of the sidewalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same full lane width as other motor vehicles.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have the right to use a full lane, just like all other vehicles.

questions.question: When should you stay farther back from the car ahead?

options.text: When driving at night
When driving on slippery roads
When driving at high speeds
All of the above

questions.explanation: Use a three-second gap in good conditions. Add one more second for each bad condition, like night driving, wet roads, or high speeds.

questions.question: What does a diamond-shaped sign mean?

options.text: There is a road hazard ahead.
You are on an interstate highway.
There is a school crossing.
This is a speed limit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is a road hazard ahead.
questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped signs are yellow or orange and warn you of dangers ahead or special rules in the area.

questions.question: What should you do at a red traffic light?

options.text: Drive through if no other cars are coming.
Keep driving because you have the right-of-way.
Stop only if a police officer is watching.
Come to a complete stop.

questions.explanation: Always come to a complete stop at a red light. It is illegal and dangerous to drive through a red light. You may turn right on red only if there is no sign that forbids it.

questions.question: What can happen when you mix alcohol with another drug?

options.text: Both the alcohol and drug effects may get stronger.
Nothing will happen.
Both the alcohol and drug effects may get weaker.
Only the alcohol effects may get weaker.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both the alcohol and drug effects may get stronger.
questions.explanation: Mixing alcohol with another drug can make both effects stronger. For example, having one drink while taking a cold medicine can affect you like you had several drinks.

questions.question: How often must vehicles be inspected?

options.text: Once every four years
Once every three years
Once every two years
Once every year

questions.explanation: Vehicles must be inspected once a year during your birth month. Schedule an appointment at an official inspection station.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: Sudden weather changes mean you need to change how you drive.
Slow down when driving in rain and fog.
Watch for cars behind you during bad weather.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: When weather changes suddenly, adjust your driving. Always slow down in rain and fog. Be alert to vehicles behind you that may be driving too fast for the conditions.

questions.question: If you drink alcohol at a social event, what keeps you safe while driving?

options.text: Drink coffee before driving.
Get a ride home with a friend who has not been drinking.
Take a cold shower before driving.
Stop drinking thirty minutes before driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get a ride home with a friend who has not been drinking.
questions.explanation: The best way to avoid impaired driving is to arrange a ride with a friend who does not drink. Coffee and cold showers do not reduce alcohol in your system or its effects. It takes about one hour for your body to process one drink.

questions.question: How does alcohol affect your driving skills and judgment?

options.text: It improves driving skills but harms judgment.
It harms both driving skills and judgment.
It does not affect either driving skills or judgment.
It does not affect judgment but harms driving skills.

questions.correctAnswerText: It harms both driving skills and judgment.
questions.explanation: Alcohol hurts the skills you need to drive safely. It slows your reaction time and reduces your ability to see clearly. It also affects your judgment about speed and distance, makes you take more risks, and lowers your caution.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: School ahead.
School crossing.
Pedestrian crossing.
Construction workers on or near the road.

questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black markings on a yellow background. They tell drivers about hazards ahead. This sign warns that people may be crossing the road.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Cars in the right lane must slow down.
No left turn.
Merge.
Pass only in the right lane.

questions.explanation: This sign means a merge is ahead. It warns that two lanes of traffic going the same direction will become one lane.

questions.question: What does alcohol do?

options.text: Slows your reflexes and reaction time.
Puts you to sleep.
Wakes you up.
Improves your judgment.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slows your reflexes and reaction time.
questions.explanation: Alcohol is a depressant that slows brain activity and harms safe driving skills. It slows reaction time and reduces good judgment.

questions.question: An eight-sided sign is always a:

options.text: Speed limit sign.
Stop sign.
Hospital sign.
Railroad warning sign.

questions.explanation: Eight-sided signs are always stop signs. Come to a full stop at every red, eight-sided sign.

questions.question: You are entering a busy freeway. What should you do to merge into traffic?

options.text: Use your mirrors and check your blind spots.
Use the entrance ramp to speed up and match freeway traffic.
Yield to traffic already on the freeway.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Use the entrance ramp to speed up to match freeway traffic and yield to cars already on the freeway. Check your mirrors and blind spots to make sure you have safe space to merge.

questions.question: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is near you, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up to get out of the way.
Stop your vehicle right away and block their path.
Do everything you can to give the emergency vehicle a clear path.
Signal to let them know when it is safe to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do everything you can to give the emergency vehicle a clear path.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is near you, you must give it a clear path. If it is safe, pull your vehicle to the side of the road so they can pass.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No left turn.
Flagger ahead.
Two-way left turn.
Turn right or go straight.

questions.explanation: This sign tells you the rules you must follow. It means you cannot turn left.

questions.question: How do you check your blind spots?

options.text: Look in your side mirrors.
Turn your head and look over your shoulders.
Look in your rearview mirror.
Look straight ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look over your shoulders.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Turn your head and look over your shoulders to check them.

questions.question: If one of your tires blows out while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Brake hard right away.
Steer straight and slow down by lifting your foot off the gas pedal.
Keep your speed the same and steer straight.
Swerve back and forth to warn other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steer straight and slow down by lifting your foot off the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: If a tire blows out, hold the steering wheel firmly and keep your car straight. Release the gas pedal slowly. Do not use the brakes until you have control. When the car is under control, brake gently and move to the side of the road safely.

questions.question: What do speed limit signs tell you?

options.text: What speeds work best for the area
The fastest and slowest speeds you are allowed to drive
The speed you should drive in heavy traffic
The speed you should drive in bad weather

questions.correctAnswerText: The fastest and slowest speeds you are allowed to drive
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs show the highest and lowest safe speeds allowed on that road. The highest speeds are for good conditions. You must drive slower when weather or road conditions are bad.

questions.question: What is the best way to reduce your risk of injury or death in a car crash?

options.text: Wear your seat belt.
Only drive on weekdays.
Stay in the right lane on highways with multiple lanes.
Only drive between 3:00 p.m. and 6:00 p.m.

questions.explanation: Wearing your seat belt is the single best thing you can do to protect yourself from serious injury or death in a crash.

questions.question: When should you always use your signal?

options.text: When changing lanes.
When pulling into or out of a parking space.
When pulling into traffic from a parking area or alley.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Always use your turn signal when you move left or right. Signal when you pull into traffic from a parking spot, change lanes, or pass another vehicle.

questions.question: When it starts to sleet or snow, you should:

options.text: Keep your windshield and mirrors clear.
Stay farther away from the vehicles in front of you.
Be careful around all other vehicles.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: In snow and ice, keep your windshield and mirrors clean. Increase the distance between your car and the vehicle ahead because your car will need more space to stop on a slippery road.

questions.question: When you are in a traffic lane on the road:

options.text: You can stop to let passengers out.
You can stop to look up an address.
You can make a U-turn or back up if you take the wrong freeway entrance.
Do not stop for any reason. Keep driving until you can safely pull off.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not stop for any reason. Keep driving until you can safely pull off.
questions.explanation: Never stop in a traffic lane for any reason. Keep moving until you can safely leave the road. If you miss your turn or exit, do not back up. Go to the next turn or exit instead.

questions.question: Which statement about seat belts and child restraints is true?

options.text: Never put a baby or small child in the front seat of a car with airbags.
An airbag can hurt a baby or small child, even in a minor crash.
All your passengers should wear seat belts or use child restraints.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Before you drive, fasten your seat belt and make sure all passengers use seat belts or child restraints. Seat belts greatly reduce the chance of serious injury or death in a crash. Children 12 and under should sit in the back seat in proper restraints. Never put a rear-facing car seat in the front with an airbag.

questions.question: You are approaching a railroad crossing and you do not see or hear a train. When must you stop?

options.text: If a stop sign is posted.
If a crossing gate is lowered.
If the crossing lights are flashing.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Always stop before crossing railroad tracks if you see flashing red lights, a lowered crossing gate, a posted stop sign, a flagger signaling you to stop, or a visible train. If you are not sure if a train is too close, stop. Never race a train.

questions.question: What can reduce road rage and aggressive driving?

options.text: Allowing extra travel time.
Obeying posted speed limits.
Using proper turn signals.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: More drivers on the road means more road rage. To help prevent it, use proper turn signals, obey speed limits, and allow extra time to reach your destination.

questions.question: Why should you not follow other cars too closely?

options.text: You may not see the road between the cars.
You may not have time to stop if the car ahead slows or stops suddenly.
You may not see the car's turn signals.
You may not see the car's brake lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may not have time to stop if the car ahead slows or stops suddenly.
questions.explanation: If you follow too closely and the car ahead suddenly slows or stops, you may not have enough time to avoid hitting it.

questions.question: What does a steady green light at an intersection mean?

options.text: You must slow down and prepare to stop.
You must stop and check for oncoming traffic before proceeding.
You may drive through if the road is clear.
You may not turn right.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may drive through if the road is clear.
questions.explanation: A steady green light means you can drive through the intersection if it is safe. You can also turn right or left on a green light unless a sign says you cannot. When turning, yield to other vehicles and pedestrians.

questions.question: Which describes an inattentive driver?

options.text: Someone who stares at objects off the road or daydreams while driving.
Someone who maintains eye contact during a conversation with a passenger while driving.
Someone who only watches the vehicle ahead.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Do not look at passengers, search for items in your vehicle, read, sightsee, or daydream while driving. Keep scanning the road, checking mirrors, and looking at your dashboard regularly. These habits keep you focused as a driver.

questions.question: If a crossing guard is directing traffic in a school zone, what must you do?

options.text: Follow the directions given by the crossing guard.
Copy what surrounding traffic is doing, despite the crossing guard's instructions.
Assume the guard is not supposed to be directing traffic.
Follow rules that would be in place if no children were present.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the directions given by the crossing guard.
questions.explanation: Be ready to slow down and drive with caution when a sign, crossing guard, or police officer tells you to. Always drive carefully in a school zone.

questions.question: You are driving on the interstate and pass your exit. What should you do?

options.text: Quickly cut across traffic to make your turn.
Make a U-turn to go back to the exit.
Continue driving and use the next exit.
Put your vehicle in reverse to go back to the exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue driving and use the next exit.
questions.explanation: Do not make a sudden turn into an exit. If you miss your exit, continue to the next one.

questions.question: You are driving when it begins to rain. What should you do?

options.text: Drive faster than surrounding traffic.
Drive at the maximum posted speed limit.
Slow down.
Drive closely behind the vehicle in front of you.

questions.explanation: When heavy rain reduces what you can see, reduce your speed. Turn on your headlights so other drivers can see you. If rain is so heavy you cannot see clearly, pull to the shoulder and stop until it improves.

questions.question: You have a green light at an intersection and pedestrians are crossing against the red. What should you do?

options.text: Honk your horn.
Speed up and pass in front of the pedestrians.
Stop to let the pedestrians cross safely.
Drive close to the pedestrians to scare them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop to let the pedestrians cross safely.
questions.explanation: Yield to pedestrians and other vehicles that may be in the intersection, even when you have a green light. Always be careful around pedestrians.

questions.question: How should you safely cross a railroad?

options.text: Look both ways only when the red light is flashing.
Listen, look both ways, then proceed if it is safe.
Cross especially quickly when a train is approaching.
Quickly pass under any lowering gates.

questions.correctAnswerText: Listen, look both ways, then proceed if it is safe.
questions.explanation: Railroad crossings are dangerous. Look and listen for trains coming from either direction before crossing. Watch for warning signals and never cross until you are certain it is safe.
